label: Jurisdictions with Approved CRISPR Therapy (Casgevy)
source: FDA (Dec 2023), EMA (Feb 2024), MHRA (Nov 2023); plus Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Canada, Switzerland
delta: US label now covers children as young as 2
deltaNote: Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) is the world's first and only approved CRISPR medicine. FDA approved a supplemental BLA on July 1, 2026 expanding eligibility from age 12+ down to age 2+ for sickle cell disease (recurrent VOCs) and transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia — the first gene therapy approved for children this young with SCD, opening eligibility to ~5,500 additional US children.

label: Active CRISPR Clinical Trials (Global)
source: ClinicalTrials.gov / IGI CRISPR Clinical Trials 2026 Update; FDA CBER Draft Guidance (Jun 2, 2026)
delta: Beam doses first patient in BEAM-302 AATD pivotal cohort (Aug 4); Fate FT839 dual-CAR T IND cleared (Jul 9)
deltaNote: Covering SCD, beta-thalassemia, cancer immunotherapy, vision, liver (ATTR, dyslipidemia, HeFH, AATD), cardiovascular, autoimmune and rare disorders. Key milestones: Beam Therapeutics dosed the first patient in the global pivotal cohort of BEAM-302 for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (Aug 4); Prime Medicine won binding arbitration confirming its right to develop PM647 in the same AATD indication, IND/CTA filing targeted Q3 2026 (Jul 8); Fate Therapeutics won FDA IND clearance for FT839, a dual CD19/CD38-targeting CAR-T therapy for autoimmune disease (Jul 9); Epicrispr completed dosing in its first-in-human EPI-321 trial for FSHD with positive interim biomarker/strength data (Jul 7); Allotera Therapeutics (formerly Wugen) raised $35M to advance its pivotal T-RRex trial of sofi-cel in T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (Jul 8). Intellia lonvo-z rolling BLA remains on track for completion in H2 2026, FDA acceptance targeted H2 2026, US launch targeted H1 2027 (per Q2 2026 update, Aug 6). Casgevy pediatric approval expanded to age 2+ on July 1, 2026.
